claims.claim: The SOLIDWORKS boom study (cad/Sim.cs Boom) is reproduced by an independent mesher and solver.
equations: K u = f, 10-node tetrahedra, 4-point Gauss, isotropic linear elasticity
beam check: sigma = M c / I, delta(x) = P x^2 (3a - x) / (6 E I)
assumptions: same geometry rules, material (E 69 GPa, nu 0.33), load and fixed root as the SOLIDWORKS study
half model with u_z = 0 on the symmetry plane
claims.tool: gmsh 4.15.2 2nd-order tetrahedra + numpy/scipy C3D10 solver (this script); SuperLU direct solve
claims.ran_evidence: solved here: 69654 DOF in 22.0 s, 190569 DOF in 777.9 s

independent_check.method: gmsh + own C3D10 solver (no SOLIDWORKS code)

claims.status_reason: tip deflection 2.652 vs 2.703 mm (-1.9 %); bending stress at x 0.10 m 25.80 vs beam 25.80 MPa (+0.03 %); root-corner peak -2.0 % (singular, not a design value); mesh change +0.04 %
limitations: verifies the computation, not the load case: the tip mass is 37 % low (STR-05) and no landing case exists (STR-11)
same idealised fixed root as SOLIDWORKS; clamp compliance is not modelled by either
claims.next_step: Re-run both solvers with the CAD lift-unit mass and a clamp-compliant root; add a landing case.
